mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X gives N items to Y', immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Treating a transfer as a one‑time net change without updating the giver's and receiver's counts for subsequent statements.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order named on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement that specifies a numeric difference.
mathgap.example: Swapping the direction and writing B − A = K.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have', translate to (A − B) = (C − D), preserving order.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing a comparison‑transfer equality that equates two signed differences.
mathgap.example: Treating the RHS as |C − D| instead of signed C − D.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement 'X has N items' fixes X's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers (if any).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a direct count statement appears in the sequence.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is the initial value regardless of earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations, simplify them, and repeat until no further substitution is possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each new assignment or simplification.
mathgap.example: Failing to propagate a newly discovered value into other equations, leaving them unsolved.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and comparative equations—to ensure no contradictions.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, before outputting the answer.
mathgap.example: Skipping the final verification step, missing a hidden inconsistency.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative and difference statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, not their starting count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing statements sequentially, respecting the order they appear.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a comparison that occurs after a transfer involving that person.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through a chain of dependencies, and ignore unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, to reduce problem size and focus on the relevant subsystem.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system when only a small part is relevant to the query.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the list of individuals and any subsequent references.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When parsing a phrase like 'the difference between the number of items that A and B have', keep the order in which A and B appear.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When translating difference‑of‑two statements into equations.
mathgap.example: Swapping A and B, turning A − B into B − A.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than"
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misreads the phrase and writes the equation B − A = K instead of A − B = K, reversing the intended relationship.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'A has K more than B' means A = B + K, i.e., A − B = K; keep the order as stated.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'difference between A and B' is interpreted as |A − B|, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the sign and order: translate 'difference between A and B' to the signed expression A − B as it appears.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are applied out of sequence or treated as a net change, causing later comparisons to use outdated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the order given, updating the giver's and receiver's counts before handling subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes any 'X has N items' sets the starting value, even if earlier transfers have already altered X's count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply a direct count statement at the point it appears, after any prior transfers, fixing the current count.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model enforces positivity on signed differences, discarding valid equations where the RHS may be negative due to other constraints.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow signed differences; only enforce positivity when the phrasing explicitly requires a positive amount (e.g., 'has K more than').
